dam-break-vof derivation

Conclusion

The surge front of the interFoam model follows the front that Martin and Moyce (1952) measured. At the 3 checked positions Z = 2.11, 3.00 and 3.89, the front of the model is 2.3 % to 3.1 % slower than the mean of the measured runs. Each difference is less than 1 standard deviation of the single runs, thus the model is in the scatter of the measurement.

The model view shows the water. alpha.water is 1 in the water and 0 in the air. Move the time slider above the view: the dot marks the front at each time of the run. The front is the largest x of a cell centre with alpha.water above 0.5, and Z = x / a with a = 2.25 in.

Result

Pass. A check passes when |computed - reference| ≤ rel_tol · |reference| + abs_tol, with rel_tol = 0.055 and abs_tol = 0 (check.toml). fh validate gives the computed values.

Made by scripts/validation-reports.py on 2026-10-27, femahoy 6f86c62-dirty.

This case checks the free surface path: a 2D dam break with the volume of fluid (VOF) method of OpenFOAM (interFoam). A water column falls on a dry floor in air, and the surge front moves along the floor. The reference is a measurement. Thus the tolerance comes from the scatter of the measurement and from the mesh and time step studies of the model.

Why this case

No other case of the suite has any of these items:

  • 2 fluids, water and air, with a sharp interface between them: the VOF method with MULES and interface compression.
  • A free surface with a large motion under gravity.
  • A start field from setFields.
  • A time step that changes with the Courant number of the flow and of the interface.
  • A transient with a value from the time history: the time at which the front gets to a position.

Source

J. C. Martin and W. J. Moyce, "Part IV. An experimental study of the collapse of liquid columns on a rigid horizontal plane", Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A 244 (1952) 312-324, https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1952.0006.

A column of water of width a and height n^2 a stands on a horizontal plane, against a wall at x = 0. At t = 0 the column is released. Table 2 (page 317) gives the times for n^2 = 2, a = 2.25 in, in the dimensionless form T = n t sqrt(g / a) = t sqrt(2 g / a) at the front positions Z = x / a. The source sets T to 1.19 at Z = 1.44 in each run ("T normalized at this value of Z"), because the instant of the release is not known exactly. The model does the same: it adds a constant to its T so that T is 1.19 at Z = 1.44.

The checks use the column "mean" for a = 2.25 in. The single runs and their standard deviation come from the same table:

CheckZMeasured T (mean)Single runsStandard deviation of the runs
T_2112.111.839, from 1.75 to 1.880.048 (2.6 %)
T_3003.002.519, from 2.38 to 2.660.099 (3.9 %)
T_3893.893.114, from 2.94 to 3.250.139 (4.5 %)

The 3 points are near the start, the middle and the end of the data that the source gives for most runs of a = 2.25 in.

Model

The OpenFOAM case is the folder n40. The units are SI.

ItemValue
Columna = 0.05715 m, height 2a, water from x = 0 to a
Tank5a long and 2.5a high: walls at x = 0, at x = 5a and at y = 0, an open top. 1 cell in z
Meshuniform square cells, dx = a / 40 = 1.43 mm. 200 x 100 = 20000 cells. n in system/blockMeshDict sets the cells across a
Fluidswater: rho = 998 kg/m^3, nu = 1e-6 m^2/s. Air: rho = 1.2 kg/m^3, nu = 1.5e-5 m^2/s. Surface tension 0.073 N/m. Laminar
SolverinterFoam with PIMPLE: 1 outer corrector, 3 pressure correctors, no momentum predictor
InterfaceMULES with interface compression cAlpha 1, MULESCorr yes, 2 corrections. Gauss vanLeer for div(phi,alpha)
MomentumGauss linearUpwind grad(U) for div(rhoPhi,U), Euler in time
Time stepadjustable, with maxCo and maxAlphaCo 0.5. 369 steps to t = 0.18 s
WallsnoSlip, fixedFluxPressure, and zeroGradient for alpha.water (a contact angle of 90 degrees)
ToptotalPressure 0 for p_rgh, pressureInletOutletVelocity for U, inletOutlet for alpha.water
Startat rest. setFields puts alpha.water = 1 in the cells of the column (boxToCell)
Frontthe largest x of a cell centre with alpha.water > 0.5. The function object front (fieldExtents) writes it after each time step
Outputat the end, the function object frontTimes (systemCall) starts awk -f system/front.awk. It writes front.txt: 1 row with the 3 values of the check. It also writes the curve front.csv for fh report --curve: the front at each step and the measured points

The run stops at t = 0.18 s. Then the front is at Z = 4.5, before the wall at x = 5a.

The front moves 1 cell at a time. Thus front.awk interpolates linearly between the 2 steps of the front on each side of x = Z a. The largest cell centre is up to 1 cell behind the surface alpha.water = 0.5. This offset is almost the same at Z = 1.44 and at the 3 points of the check, thus the normalization removes most of it. The mesh study includes the remainder.

The front of the model gets to Z = 1.44 at T = 0.91: the release of the model is instantaneous. The constant that sets T to 1.19 is thus 0.28.

Studies

These commands, in the repository root, solve the case with other values in a scratch folder. On Linux, use openfoam2512 in place of openfoam:

cp -R validation/cases/dam-break-vof/n40 /tmp/dam && cd /tmp/dam
sed -i.orig 's/^n       40;/n       80;/' system/blockMeshDict
openfoam blockMesh && openfoam setFields && openfoam interFoam

The values are in /tmp/dam/front.txt.

Tolerance

The tolerance is rel_tol = 0.055 and abs_tol = 0.

CauseBasisEffect
The scatter of the measurementThe largest standard deviation of the single runs about the mean (at Z = 3.89, 4 runs)4.5 %
Mesh error of the modelThe largest difference between n = 40 and n = 80 (T_389)0.5 %
Time step error of the modelThe largest difference between the Courant numbers 0.5 and 0.25 (T_389)0.2 %

rel_tol is the sum, 5.2 %, rounded up to 5.5 %. The front of the model is slower than the mean at all 3 points, by 2.3 % to 3.1 %. Each difference is less than 1 standard deviation of the runs.

The tolerance stops this error:

  • A column of height a in place of 2a (a wrong box in system/setFieldsDict): T is 1.924, 2.730 and 3.482. T_300 (8.8 % too large) and T_389 (12 %) fail.

The tolerance does not stop a coarse mesh: n = 10 passes, because the time of the front changes little with the mesh.

Not in the check

  • The height of the column at x = 0 (Table 6 of the source). The table of the function object front has it: the largest y of the water.
  • Z larger than 4.11: only 3 of the 9 runs of a = 2.25 in have data there, and the run takes longer.
  • The other column of the source, a = 1.125 in: it has the same n^2 and thus the same T(Z) in theory.

On a Mac with 10 cores and other jobs, fh validate of the case took 85 s (34 s of CPU time) on 1 core with OpenFOAM v2512.
